metadata.purpose: Transform each incoming value through a supplied projection without changing its delivery policy.

cardinality.signature: map : (T! x Index! -> R!) -> T* -> R*
conditions: One output per successfully returned projection while the subscription remains active; throwing produces an error instead.
Signatures describe successful value flow, not guarantees against errors or cancellation.
The full callback receives a zero-based source-notification index. Filter runtime truthiness is modeled even though its usual TypeScript predicate returns boolean.

scope.parameters: A named callback binding; nonnegative safe-integer callback indices below overflow
scope.callbacks: Callback invocation is an action; return/throw is a correlated input. No callback function runs inside a guard, reaction, validator, or generator.
scope.time: No timer or clock is introduced. Calling is a synchronous logical phase, not a scheduled delay; example sequence numbers order same-frame events.
scope.reentrancy: Non-reentrant source, callback and observer behavior; cancellation only between fully resolved value reactions.
exclusions: Deprecated thisArg overload and invalid non-function callback arguments.
Nested notifications or cancellation inside callbacks or observer delivery; throwing observers or finalizers.
Counter precision loss beyond the safe-integer domain; proof of TypeScript predicate narrowing.
A production callback/effect interpreter, runtime snapshot codec, or callback purity guarantee.

initialization.sourceSubscription: Acquire exactly one source subscription; no invocation before its first next.

ownership.sharing: No sharing introduced. Each result subscription has its own index, even with a shared or hot producer.
ownership.reset: A fresh execution starts at index zero. Closed executions have no admissible inputs.

resources.owner: external binding; invocation identity belongs to this execution

dispatch.actionSemantics: Source next creates one invoke-callback request, with its pre-increment index. Only its correlated return/throw is admissible while Calling. Resolve it before another external input; no callback is executed by the specification runner.
cancellationCheckpoints: Active between resolved source reactions; release upstream without complete.
Cancellation during Calling or downstream notification delivery requires a refined profile and is excluded.

actions: subscribe to the source without invoking the callback
rules.explanation: Subscribing to map connects to the source and starts a fresh callback index at zero. Constructing the pipeline does not invoke the callback.

actions: request exactly one callback invocation with the incoming value and the current zero-based index
rules.nextState: calling with the input retained and the next index increased by one
rules.explanation: Each incoming value invokes the supplied function once with that value and its zero-based source index. The index advances for every invocation, independently of whether a value is subsequently forwarded.

actions: forward the returned result as one value
rules.nextState: active with the next callback index
rules.explanation: A successful projection result is forwarded as exactly one value, including undefined, an object, or an Observable. Map does not flatten or subscribe to the returned value.
If the supplied function throws, the thrown value is sent through the error channel and the source subscription is released. The failing input produces no next notification and no completion follows.
Source completion is forwarded without invoking the callback or creating another value. The source subscription is released.
A source error is forwarded unchanged without invoking the callback. It releases the source subscription and is not followed by completion.

actions: release the source subscription without notifying downstream
rules.explanation: Downstream cancellation releases the source subscription and stops further callback invocations. Cancellation does not emit completion.
